title: Run evaluation
description:
Written by `persona-evaluator`. This file is the meta-layer the rest of the pipeline lacks: an assessment not of the product, but of whether this run is trustworthy evidence about the product (DESIGN.md section 4).

Note the apparent inconsistency with session-record.schema.json, which forbids verdict fields: this schema has `trust.verdict`. That is deliberate and not a contradiction. The prohibition is on an agent certifying its own work. persona-evaluator judges a session it did not run, about an app it never touched.

consistency.description: Drift is progressive, so the halves are scored separately. A single whole-session score averages the drift away and reports a healthy-looking number for a run that fell apart at step 20.

dimensions.description: Component scores. Separated because they fail independently: an agent can keep the persona's vocabulary perfectly while troubleshooting with a patience the persona does not have.

lexical_violations.description: Copied from `pqa drift`, which is a deterministic string match. Included here so the evaluator's soft judgment and the hard check sit side by side in one file.

injection_steps.description: Steps at which the persona summary was re-injected.

behavioral_notes.description: Drift the string check cannot see: an agent that avoids every forbidden term while still behaving like an engineer. This is the only guard against behavioural drift, and it is a soft one.

verdict.description: 'degraded' means the findings are usable but the coverage claim is not: the run stopped behaving like the persona partway through, so what it did NOT find says nothing.

usable_through_step.description: For a degraded run: the last step at which the agent was still in character. Findings after this point are still real, but they are a QA engineer's findings, not this persona's.
